patch.value: History maintenance rewrites hold a plain lock, not a fenced lease, so a rewrite can commit after its lock expired and another writer took it over

Found by CodeRabbit on PR 1654. executeHistoryRewrite in src/core/history/history-rewrite.ts acquires the item lock with acquireLock and calls applyRewrite directly. Ordinary item commits use acquireLockLease and lease.fence (pm-gh1549), which refuses a commit whose lock generation was taken over after a TTL expiry. history-redact, history-repair and history-compact therefore lack that fence. A rewrite that stalls past the lock TTL can still write the item document and history stream after another writer acquired the lock, and the drift and expected-revision checks it ran earlier then no longer describe what it overwrites. This predates PR 1654. The expected-revision check added there runs under this same lock, so it inherits the gap.

executeHistoryRewrite acquires a LockLease and runs every persisted rewrite step through lease.fence, releasing it in finally; A rewrite whose lease generation was taken over refuses with lock_lost and writes neither the item nor the history stream; Regression test forces a takeover between the drift check and applyRewrite for history-redact
History maintenance commits only while its lock generation is still its own, like item commits
history-redact/repair/compact hold a plain acquireLock lock and commit without a lease fence
